newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan May money supply in line with forecast-BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan May money supply in line with forecast-BOJ.

text.p: The growth in Japan's money supply in May was in line with forecasts, a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said on Wednesday.
The BOJ said earlier that Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs) grew a preliminary 3.0 percent in May from a year earlier.
"The rise was within the range of the BOJ's forecast that it (the growth of M2 plus CD) would be around three percent during the April-June period," said the BOJ official.
"There is no big change in the trend (of the money supply growth)," he added.
The BOJ said the M2 plus CDs growth for April was revised up to a 3.2 rise from a preliminary 3.1 percent rise.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected the May figure to grow by 2.9 percent to 3.3 percent from a year earlier.
An economist at DKB Research said the sales tax rise in April, which pushed up domestic prices and increased circulation of money, might have helped support money supply growth.
But bank lending remained sluggish and slowed the growth in money supply. "Bank lending unexpectedly stayed weak," the economist added.
